ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding and periodically thereafter, identify domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates, and screen relevant parties and beneficial owners against applicable EU and UN restrictive measures and Spanish national measures. OFAC screening is not generally a Spanish statutory requirement but is appropriate where there is a US nexus, US-dollar clearing, or relevant contractual or banking exposure. Apply risk-based customer due diligence, source-of-funds and, where warranted, source-of-wealth checks, enhanced due diligence for higher-risk relationships, and documented escalation and ongoing monitoring under Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014. Payment-platform rules may impose additional checks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), official online corporate-name reservation service (Sección de Denominaciones).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be distinguishable from names already registered or reserved and comply with Spanish company-name rules, including Royal Decree 1784/1996. It must include the legal-form indication Sociedad Limitada, Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, or an accepted abbreviation such as S.L. A name may use a foreign-language expression if it is legally acceptable and sufficiently distinguishable. Local-language and transliteration requirements may apply to names containing non-Latin characters; confirm the RMC's technical and documentary requirements before filing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or confusingly similar to existing or reserved corporate names
Terms that conflict with law, public order, or good customs
Terms that may mislead as to the company's activity, nature, or legal form
Official or institutional names and terms implying public authority, government sponsorship, or a regulated status without authorization
Regulated professional, financial, insurance, banking, or other reserved terms where use requires authorization or could mislead
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Request an alternative-name certificate from the RMC and verify the certificate's stated validity and renewal conditions; the standard certificate is generally effective for three months for execution of the deed, while reservation of the name may be maintained for up to six months. If rejected, obtain the reason, submit a new application with materially distinct alternatives or request reconsideration from the RMC. A registral decision may be challenged through the remedies and deadlines stated in the decision and applicable registry legislation, including an appeal to the Directorate General for Legal Security and Public Faith where available. Confirm the specific remedy and deadline in the rejection notice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An SL must have a registered domicile in Spain under the Companies Act (Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010). A virtual office may be acceptable as a registered address if the company has its effective administration and management there or its principal establishment or operation there, and the address can satisfy registry, tax, banking, and service-of-process requirements. A mail-only address may be inadequate for banking, tax, AML, or substance assessments. Digital publishing and webtoon syndication do not, on the stated facts, require a sector-specific operating license; consumer, intellectual-property, data-protection, tax, and platform obligations remain applicable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No general statutory percentage is published. Risk is not reliably quantifiable; Spanish tax, registry, law-enforcement, or AML authorities may conduct verification or request evidence of the registered domicile and activity. Banks and payment providers may also require an address check or supporting evidence. Maintain accessible premises or a demonstrably compliant registered-office arrangement and accurate business records.

stage_2.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable. Digital webtoon syndication (ISIC 9000 / NAICS 511130) is an intangible service not assimilated to an industrial plant. The only territorial window is the municipal Ayuntamiento for a standard responsible declaration of activity for administrative offices and, if staff are engaged, the Seguridad Social registration. No provincial industrial or mining/energy license is triggered.
stage_2.operating_license_title: None required. A municipal Declaración Responsable de Inicio de Actividad (responsible declaration of commencement) per Ley 12/2012 (licence-free start for non-polluting, small-audience activities) suffices, provided the office is under the thresholds of Ley 12/2012 Annex and the urban plan (PGOUM) classifies the street for office use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the AEAT Sede Electrónica. The AEAT administers Spanish tax identification, census registration, Value Added Tax (VAT), Corporate Income Tax, non-resident taxation, the Register of Intra-Community Operators (ROI), and the Spanish VAT Information Exchange System (VIES).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) through AEAT census registration using Modelo 036 after incorporation documentation is available, followed by the definitive NIF after registration with the Mercantile Registry and submission of the registered deed and updated corporate particulars. A foreign entity requiring a Spanish NIF files Modelo 036 with AEAT and submits evidence of legal existence, constitutional documents, identification of directors or legal representatives, proof of authority, and, where applicable, a Spanish tax representative or authorized agent. Foreign public documents generally require apostille or legalization and an official Spanish translation. VAT registration is performed through the same census process; registration in the ROI and activation of an NIF-VAT for intra-Community transactions require a specific request and supporting evidence of intended intra-Community activity. The NIF-VAT normally uses the Spanish NIF preceded by the country code ES. A foreign digital-services supplier may also need Spanish VAT registration or Union One Stop Shop registration depending on customer location and the applicable place-of-supply rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no general United States-style check-the-box election for Spanish limited liability companies. An SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person. Tax transparency applies only to specifically regulated forms and situations, such as certain civil entities without commercial purpose or qualifying economic interest group regimes. Spanish tax law contains targeted elections and regimes, including tax consolidation, special restructuring treatment, certain holding-company participation exemptions, and special regimes for qualifying entities, but these do not convert an ordinary SL into a fiscally transparent entity. Spanish and EU anti-hybrid-mismatch rules may deny deductions, include income, or otherwise neutralize hybrid outcomes; they are statutory anti-abuse rules rather than elective entity-classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA) under Law 37/1992 and related regulations. Spanish VAT applies in mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands. The Canary Islands are outside the EU VAT territory and generally apply the Canary Islands General Indirect Tax (IGIC); Ceuta and Melilla are also outside Spanish VAT territory and have separate indirect-tax treatment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general annual turnover threshold applies to Spanish-established businesses for ordinary VAT registration. A taxable person must register through the census declaration before commencing economic activity, making taxable supplies, or carrying out transactions requiring a Spanish VAT number. The EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold applies to specified intra-Community cross-border business-to-consumer supplies of goods and telecommunications, broadcasting and electronically supplied services, subject to the relevant Union One Stop Shop rules; it is not a general Spanish VAT-registration threshold. For a Spanish SL supplying digital comics, VAT treatment depends on the customer location, customer status, platform contractual model, and whether Apple or Google is the deemed supplier.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance system for all businesses. Immediate Supply of Information (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) applies principally to businesses with turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups, entities in the monthly VAT refund regime, and other specified taxpayers; qualifying taxpayers submit VAT ledger data electronically to AEAT, generally within four calendar days, subject to statutory exceptions. Spanish invoicing systems must comply with the certified-system and anti-manipulation requirements under applicable invoicing legislation, including the Veri*Factu framework and its implementation timetable. The Business Creation and Growth Law establishes mandatory electronic invoicing between businesses, but operational scope and effective dates depend on implementing regulations. Electronic invoicing is not equivalent to universal pre-clearance. Invoices issued through Apple App Store or Google Play Billing must be assessed against the platform's merchant-of-record, deemed-supplier, invoicing, commission, and VAT-reporting arrangements. B2C electronically supplied services are generally taxed where the consumer is established, domiciled, or habitually resident, subject to the applicable EU rules and OSS reporting.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law, provided the supplier can substantiate the export and satisfy the statutory conditions. The exemption is not an automatic commercial export rate and requires documentary evidence linking the supplier, goods, purchaser, transport, and customs export. Services supplied to business customers established outside Spain are generally analyzed under the business-to-business place-of-supply rule and may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT rather than zero-rated. Electronically supplied services to consumers are generally taxed according to the consumer's location; non-EU consumer supplies may be outside Spanish VAT where the statutory place-of-supply rules are satisfied. Digital webtoon licensing, syndication, and platform supplies therefore require a separate analysis of contractual rights, customer status, platform principal status, and actual use or enjoyment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For exported goods: electronic export customs declaration or equivalent customs exit confirmation, including the Movement Reference Number where applicable
Customs exit result or other AEAT- and customs-accepted evidence that the goods physically left EU customs territory
Commercial invoice, sales or licensing contract, packing list where relevant, transport document such as Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR, and evidence identifying the supplier and exported goods
Evidence of payment and customer identity where relevant to establish the transaction and audit trail

For digital services: customer location evidence, customer VAT number or business-status evidence where applicable, platform or merchant-of-record agreement, transaction reports, payment records, IP or billing-address evidence where legally permissible, and OSS or VAT return records

An Inward Remittance Certificate is not a general statutory Spanish requirement for claiming export VAT exemption, and Spain has no general foreign-exchange certification requirement comparable to jurisdictions that mandate a bank remittance certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export VAT treatment. AEAT may deny the exemption or refund, reassess output VAT, recover improperly refunded input VAT, and charge late-payment interest if export departure, customer location, service classification, or transaction authenticity is not substantiated. VAT underpayment penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount depending on the applicable infringement category, concealment, fraud, and aggravating factors; separate penalties may apply for inaccurate returns, defective invoices, failure to maintain records, or obstruction of inspection. Voluntary late correction may reduce applicable penalties and interest where statutory conditions are met. Fraudulent or fictitious transactions can trigger criminal tax proceedings where the statutory criminal thresholds and intent requirements are satisfied, including the Spanish Penal Code tax-fraud threshold generally based on an evaded amount exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax period and tax. Any export exemption or refund obtained without valid evidence may be clawed back with the reassessed VAT, interest, and applicable penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); foreign-investment statistical and registration administration is coordinated with the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business through the Foreign Investment Registry (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain, as a Eurozone member, operates a fully liberalized convertibility regime for both current account and capital account transactions. There is no exchange-control approval requirement for payments, profit remittances, royalties, license fees, or capital movements among EU/EEA residents and third countries, pursuant to Article 63 TFEU and the OECD Codes of Liberalisation. Foreign direct investment into a Spanish SL, including share capital subscription, shareholder loans, and participative loans (préstamos participativos), is generally free and subject only to ex-post statistical declaration to the Foreign Investment Registry, with prior screening required only in sensitive sectors under Royal Decree-Law 34/2020 (as amended) and Regulation (EU) 2019/452. Profit remittance hurdles are fiscal rather than monetary: dividend distributions require a shareholders' resolution and compliance with the Capital Companies Act solvency balance-sheet test; outbound dividends and royalties to non-residents attract Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) withholding at 19% (or 24% where no treaty applies), which may be reduced under double taxation treaties or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive mechanics. No central-bank prior authorization or conversion certificate is required for any treasury remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Spanish and EU law impose no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline, no repatriation deadline, and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts, including Apple IAP and Google Play Billing platform remittances, may be held in EUR or in freely convertible foreign currency in resident or non-resident accounts. The only related obligation is statistical: the receiving bank records the transaction for Banco de España balance-of-payments statistics and applies the corresponding transaction purpose code; no further authorization or surrender procedure exists for a Spanish SL.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for EEA-licensed electronic money institutions that passport into Spain and can issue an EU IBAN with SEPA and SWIFT access; Low for offshore non-EEA digital EMIs. Legal constraints: under Law 21/2010 (electronic money) and Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2), only an EMI authorized in an EEA member state and passporting into Spain may lawfully provide e-money and payment accounts to a Spanish SL without a separate Spanish license. Offshore digital EMIs (for example UK, Singapore, or US-based) cannot serve as the primary treasury account holder for the SL; they may be used only as supplementary FX and payout channels routed through the primary EEA bank or EMI. All providers, including EMIs, must apply the Spanish AML/CFT framework of Law 10/2010, including UBO identification and ongoing monitoring. The recommended structure is a Tier-1 Spanish bank as anchor account with an EEA-passported EMI overlay for API-based virtual-account management and cross-border FX.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is not statutorily mandated under Spanish AML law; Law 10/2010 requires reliable client and beneficial-owner identification rather than face-to-face contact. In bank practice, resident directors and managers can open an SL account fully remotely using video identification, qualified electronic signature, the notarized deed of incorporation, a valid NIF tax certificate, and Registro Mercantil officer certificates. Non-resident directors face a stricter bank-policy hurdle: most Tier-1 banks require either (i) a physical interview at a Spanish branch, (ii) a notarized and apostilled power of attorney granted to a Spanish resident attorney-in-fact, or (iii) video-identification accepted only for EU/EEA nationals with a clean sanctions and PEP profile. Fully remote opening for a 100% non-resident-owned creative-services SL is generally unavailable without a senior compliance override; a practical route is provisional remote onboarding at an EEA EMI plus a branch confirmation meeting at the Tier-1 bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and chain-of-control opacity: the SL is owned by a multi-country syndicate of shareholders across the EU, Latin America, and Asia, with webtoon content rights co-licensed through intermediate holding vehicles, making the beneficial owner not immediately identifiable.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized deed of incorporation, current Registro Mercantil certificate of incorporation and officer appointments, a Spanish-law UBO declaration identifying every natural person with direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more, a full corporate-ownership organizational chart, passports or national IDs of all UBOs and directors, and certified corporate-registry extracts and apostilled translations for each foreign corporate shareholder in the chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds concern for the initial share-capital injection received from non-EU, high-risk, or tax-haven-adjacent jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 trace and paying-bank reference identifying the exact shareholder account, six months of bank statements of the contributing shareholder, signed source-of-wealth and source-of-funds memoranda, tax residence certificates of each investor, and transactional documents proving lawful origin of funds, including sale agreements, financing agreements, dividend resolutions, or prior employment/asset-acquisition documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated-platform settlement red flag: the SL's primary revenue is received from Apple App Store In-App Purchase and Google Play Billing, being market-place aggregates with no end-customer detail, which can be perceived as unidentified counterparty proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console enrollment certificates showing the SL as the named legal beneficiary and account holder, six months of platform payout remittance reports, Apple and Google commission and VAT invoices, EU VAT OSS electronic-distribution declarations, the webtoon content catalog and digital-distribution contracts, and an internally reconciled ledger mapping each platform payout to specific chapter-episode unlocking sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party IP royalty outflows to non-resident co-licensors, which may be benchmarked as transfer-pricing aggression or undisguised dividend distributions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed licensing and syndication agreements with arm's-length royalty rates justified under OECD transfer-pricing methods, comparable-license or profit-split benchmark study, trademark and copyright registrations with OEPM, and completed related-party transaction annexes in the Spanish corporate tax return (Form 232) together with the annual Form 200 filing position.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening hits on Latin American distribution platforms, payment aggregators, or fractional syndicate shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date EU, OFAC, and UN consolidated sanctions screening reports for all counterparties, UBOs, and connected payment processors, executed PEP declarations and Law 10/2010 risk-rating questionnaires, the Apple/Google KYC files evidencing their own compliance due diligence, and an external counsel legal memorandum assessing residual risk and identifying defensive monitoring measures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Step 1: The non-resident shareholder executes a SWIFT MT103 (plus MT202 COVER for high-value transfers) from its own bank account into the SL's blocked capital-formation account (cuenta de constitución) opened at the Spanish Tier-1 bank in the name of the company being incorporated, referencing the SL's provisional NIF tax number and stating 'aporte de capital social – escritura de constitución'. Step 2: The bank applies Banco de España balance-of-payments coding and blocks the funds until the deed of incorporation is registered in the Registro Mercantil. Step 3: Foreign direct investment must be declared to the Foreign Investment Registry (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores) within one month of execution where the investment exceeds EUR 3,005,000, or where the foreign investor's participation reaches 10% or more of share capital and the company's net worth exceeds EUR 3,005,000; smaller injections are captured statistically by the bank. Step 4: Where the investor is a non-EU/EFTA party, treasury counsel must confirm that no prior authorization is triggered under Royal Decree-Law 34/2020 sensitive-sector screening, which may encompass media and communication-related undertakings. Step 5: Subsequent capital increases, shareholder loans, and participatory-loan injections follow the same MT103 protocol with purpose codes reflecting the operation; the SL must reject all crypto-denominated or third-party commingled transfers as automatic compliance blockers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Eurozone and SEPA disbursements: standard royalty, artist-fee, and operational payments use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) cleared through TARGET2 with T+0/T+1 execution, with SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) available for time-critical payouts. Non-euro disbursements: SWIFT MT103 or MT103 STP via the Spanish bank's correspondent network for USD, GBP, MXN, ARS, KRW, and other currencies, with the EUR counterpart converted through the bank's FX desk or executed against an outstanding FX forward. High-value bank-to-bank cover: SWIFT MT202 COVER where applicable. Trade-based settlement: for ISIC 9000's ancillary merchandise, print, and co-branding business, a Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP 600 (SWIFT MT700) or a Standby Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT760) is permissible; pure digital webtoon syndication does not warrant letter-of-credit usage. Platform servicing: Apple IAP and Google Play Billing payouts are wired or merchant-of-record settled directly into the SL's operational account, with reconciliation against developer-console financial reports. Treasury efficiency: zero-balancing sweeps across the Tier-1 bank's EUR account and multi-currency sub-accounts, with the EEA EMI used as a supplementary FX top-up channel only.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/KRW, EUR/GBP) executed under ISDA/EMTA master documentation with Banco de España-regulated Spanish bank counterparties, hedged against forecast Apple/Google platform revenue streams.

Non-deliverable forward contracts (NDFs) for inconvertible or restricted currencies, notably Argentine peso (ARS) for Latin American market proceeds, cash-settled in EUR or USD against a reference fixing and booked only through licensed bank counterparties with appropriate regulatory capacity.

FX swaps and rollover swaps to net Apple/Google USD payout receipts against USD-denominated royalty payables while preserving the SL's EUR treasury position and avoiding speculative balance-sheet exposure.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCS) for balance-sheet hedging of intercompany Euro/USD financing and shareholder loans, documented under ISDA 2002/2013 CSA standards and compliant with Spanish corporate thin-capitalization and transfer-pricing rules.

Purchased vanilla FX options (put and call structures) to cap downside on Latin American revenue repatriation while retaining upside benefit, subject to board-approved hedge-policy memoranda and supported by hedged underlying cash flows.

Natural and operational hedging techniques permissible without Banco de España authorization, including multi-currency account holding, invoicing webtoon licensing in EUR or USD to match payable currencies, and intercompany netting with the parent syndication vehicle.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Cuentas Anuales (Deposit of Annual Accounts)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (via Depósito de Cuentas Digital platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved at an Ordinary General Meeting within six months of fiscal year-end; deposit with the Mercantile Registry within one month after approval. For calendar-year SL: approval by June 30, deposit by July 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cierre registral blocks registration of all corporate acts until accounts are filed; administrative fines of EUR 200–20,000 may be imposed based on total assets and turnover; continued default can lead to court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración del Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax Return, Form 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days following the six-month anniversary of the end of the tax period; for a fiscal year ending December 31, the filing date is July 25.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without prior demand triggers a 5% surcharge on the tax due plus late-payment interest (3.75% in 2024); formal non-filing after administrative request can result in penalties of 50%–100% of the outstanding tax amount, and possible criminal tax consequences for fraud.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración Anual de Titular Real (Annual Beneficial Owner Reconfirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (as part of the annual accounts filing package or accompanying form)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed simultaneously with the annual accounts deposit; calendar-year SL by July 31. Changes in beneficial ownership during the year must be notified within 15 days of the transfer by public deed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or update beneficial ownership information violates AML legislation and may attract fines up to EUR 60,000 or more; registry acts may also be suspended until compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SL must appoint an auditor if, for two consecutive fiscal years, it meets at least two of the following: balance-sheet total exceeds EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; average number of employees exceeds 50. The obligation ceases when the thresholds cease to be met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) approved by Real Decreto 1514/2007; IFRS-EU is mandatory for consolidated groups and listed companies but not for a standalone unlisted SL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must deposit an updated 'declaración de titular real' with the Registro Mercantil concurrently with the annual accounts. Share transfers and ownership changes are effective only after public deed registration and the updated beneficial-owner form is filed within 15 days. No change during the year still requires implicit reconfirmation through the annual deposit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro Registro de Socios (Register of Members)
Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales (Inventory and Annual Accounts Book)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General statutory rate 25% (art. 29.1 Ley 27/2014 LIS). Newly incorporated SLs carrying on an economic activity may apply 15% to the first EUR 300,000 of positive taxable base in the first two taxable periods with profit, 25% on the excess. R&D&I tax credits: 25% on qualifying research and development expenses and 8%-12% on technological innovation. Article 36.2 LIS audiovisual/animation production incentives: 20% credit on the first EUR 1,000,000 and 10% on the excess for foreign productions filmed in Spain; 15%/5% for domestic producers. The digital services tax (3%) does not apply below EUR 3,000,000 Spanish revenue and EUR 750,000,000 worldwide group revenue thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed exclusively through the AEAT Sede Electrónica (RED/SAR system) using digital certificate, cl@ve PIN or authorised representative. Quarterly instalment payments are declared on Modelo 202 (calendar-year taxpayers: April 20, October 20, December 20).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end. For an SL with a 31 December year-end, the filing window is 1-25 July.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resultado contable: net accounting profit before tax per the SL's Spanish GAAP financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Spanish SL's full-year worldwide result if effective management is in Spain. For a permanent establishment of a foreign entity, enter the Spanish-branch result only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Correcciones al resultado contable: permanent and temporary book-tax adjustments (non-deductible expenses, amortisation differences, timing items).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support all upward/downward adjustments with Spanish documentation; head-office cost allocations must satisfy art. 18.1 LIS and OECD transfer pricing guidelines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base imponible: taxable income before application of prior-year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents without a Spanish permanent establishment do not file Modelo 200; their Spanish-source income is subject to withholding and reported on Modelo 210.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compensación de bases imponibles negativas: offset of accumulated negative tax bases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carryforward is unlimited. Annual offset is capped at 50% for net turnover of EUR 20M-60M and 25% above EUR 60M; a minimum of EUR 1,000,000 per year may always be offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cuota íntegra: gross tax liability at 25% (or 15% on the first EUR 300,000 for newly created SLs in the first two positive-base years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same gross rates apply to permanent establishments; no deemed-cost deduction applies for functions performed by the foreign head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deducciones para incentivos y bonificaciones: R&D&I credits and Article 36 LIS audiovisual/animation production credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are available only for qualifying activity physically performed in Spain; foreign productions require prior MINCOTUR certification of the production's eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cuota líquida, pagos a cuenta and result to settle: net tax payable or refund due after Modelo 202 instalments and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund due to the Spanish SL is paid to the Spanish account; distributions of profits to non-resident shareholders are separately subject to 19% IRNR withholding via Modelo 216.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior tax authority request: surcharge of 5% (within 3 months) rising by 1% per month to 15%-20% after 12 months, plus statutory late-payment interest. Formal breach of filing obligation: fixed penalty of EUR 200 per return (art. 198.1 LGT). Omission or false data causing non-payment: proportional penalty of 50%-150% of the amount (art. 191 LGT). Criminal referral applies where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax year.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on dividends and other profit distributions from the Spanish SL to non-resident shareholders (art. 25.1.f) Real Decreto Legislativo 5/2004 IRNR and art. 61 LIS).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced or zero rate under a double tax agreement, the beneficial owner must deliver a duly legalised Certificate of Fiscal Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority to the Spanish SL as withholding agent before payment. The agent may apply the treaty rate at source or the non-resident may obtain a refund by filing Modelo 210 attaching the TRC, supporting bank statements and a declaration of beneficial ownership. Claims are subject to the four-year prescription period; the AEAT applies the MLI principal-purpose test to deny treaty access to conduit arrangements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties from the cross-border licence of webtoon content: statutory withholding 19% on gross Spanish-source income; most Spanish tax treaties reduce the rate to 10% (e.g., Spain-United States, Spain-United Kingdom), with certain cultural copyright royalties eligible for 5% under bilateral treaties. Interest: statutory 19%, generally reduced to 10% under most Spanish DTAs.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File are mandatory where the SL's net turnover (importe neto de la cifra de negocios) equals or exceeds EUR 45,000,000 or where the taxpayer belongs to a tax group with consolidated turnover of at least that amount. Documentation is also required without turnover threshold for transactions with entities in non-cooperative (Spanish blacklist) jurisdictions. Country-by-Country Report applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000, which also triggers the Pillar Two 15% minimum top-up tax rules as transposed in Spain.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price for webtoon chapter licensing and platform commissions)
Resale Price Method (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing distribution arrangements)
Cost Plus Method (webtoon production and translation services)
TNMM (routine Spanish marketing and localisation functions)
Profit Split (high-value integrated IP ownership and development operations)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Under art. 8 LIS, a Spanish SL is tax-resident if incorporated in Spain or if its place of effective management is in Spain. The AEAT rejects letterbox or conduit structures: the company must demonstrate real personnel, premises, decision-making and commercial functions. Absence of substance triggers art. 15 LGT general anti-abuse recharacterisation, the Spanish CFC rules (arts. 100-103 LIS) for passive digital income, the civil doctrine of levantamiento del velo, and denial of treaty benefits under the BEPS MLI principal-purpose test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion (Delito contra la Hacienda Pública, art. 305 CP)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly underreporting webtoon revenue settled through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing, recording platform settlements net rather than gross, shifting profits to a zero-tax affiliate lacking economic substance, or failing to file Modelo 200 / Modelo 202 with a defrauded amount exceeding EUR 120,000 in a single tax year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment from one to six years, a fine of two to six times the defrauded amount, loss of grants and tax benefits for up to four years, and publication of the criminal judgment. Administrative claw-back adds a 50%-150% late-filing/proportional penalty plus statutory late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable as participants under art. 31 CP. Under art. 42 LGT they are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax debts when their intent or gross negligence caused the non-payment. Courts may order preventive seizure of personal assets, travel bans (prohibición de salida del territorio nacional) and passport withdrawal during the investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / absence of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Spanish SL with no employees, no office, no commercial functions or bank accounts in Spain, formally transferring the webtoon IP to a zero-rate jurisdiction while all decision-making occurs from shareholders' personal addresses abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may recharacterise the entity as tax-resident in Spain under art. 8.2 LIS if effective management is in Spain, attribute passive income to shareholders under the CFC rules, deny treaty benefits, and reassess intercompany payments at arm's length plus 15% transfer pricing surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Spanish doctrine of levantamiento del velo allows creditors and the tax authority to hold directors and controlling shareholders personally liable for the entity's debts where the corporate form is used as a screen. Where the artificiality conceals income, directors face aggravated criminal liability under art. 305.2 CP with increased prison terms.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / CTF and anonymous payment structures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing webtoon settlement payments through unregistered crypto-wallets or prepaid quasi-cash instruments above the EUR 10,000 monitoring threshold, failing to register with SEPBLAC where virtual-currency exchange services are provided, or structuring (smurfing) payments into multiple low-value transfers to avoid transparency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 10/2010 as amended by Law 7/2021: very serious infringements carry fines from EUR 150,000 to EUR 1,500,000 or up to three times the value of the services, plus prohibition from public contracting, suspension of authorisation and publication of the sanctioning resolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors qualify as sujetos obligados and may be personally sanctioned where the breach is attributable to their gross negligence. Criminal money-laundering proceedings under art. 301 CP can result in seizure, travel bans and imprisonment for directors who knowingly process illicit platform proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing irregularities and abusive intercompany royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying artificially inflated management or royalty fees to a related foreign entity for the licence of the webtoon catalogue without an arm's-length economic analysis, without a group transfer pricing policy, or without the statutory Local/Master File once the EUR 45,000,000 turnover threshold is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may recharacterise the transactions at market value under art. 18.4 LIS, disallow the excess expenditure, and impose documentation penalties of EUR 1,500 per data item for omitted information and EUR 150 per item for inaccurate data, together with proportional penalties on the uncovered tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or executed the non-arm's length arrangements are jointly and severally liable for the resulting tax debt under art. 43.1.a) LGT. In cases involving false invoices, directors additionally face the criminal offence of falsificación de documentos mercantiles with imprisonment of six months to six years.
